name: Dark Sage
lede: Dark Sage is a muted, greyish green, a shade down from [[sage]] and classed by the ISCC-NBS system as a moderate yellowish green.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
No book in our library records a name at this position before the xkcd color survey of 2010, where the public supplied the plain descriptive phrase "dark sage" [1]. Its origin before that survey is undocumented here [1].

The nearest ISCC-NBS 1955 block is moderate yellowish green, under 5 CIEDE2000 units away, with a Munsell reading near 9.9GY in hue [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[hay-s-green]], [[mineral-green]] and [[emeraude]], at 2.8, 3.9 and 4.2 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for this swatch in 57 of 23,781 paintings, as photographed [2]. Félix Vallotton's *Corn Fields* (1900) carries the most of it, covering 50 per cent of the canvas, and Claude Monet's own works carry it 25 times the archive's baseline rate [2]. Its peak decade is the 1910s, and the word "Viridian" shares its canvases far more than chance [2]. Where it appears, it most often sits as a mid-tone rather than a shadow or a highlight [2].
